review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how the simp lemmas fit together: mem_coe, mem_coeIdeal, mem_coeSubmodule, coe_coeIdeal, coe_zero, coeIdeal_bot, sup_eq_add, coe_add and coe_inf. I opened IsLocalization.coeSubmodule in Localization/Submodule.lean. I grepped for uses of coeToSubmodule_eq_bot, coe_natCast and coe_nsmul. I found no rewrite cycle and no unsuitable orientation. The sup/add normal form (sup_eq_add, coe_add, coeIdeal_sup) looks consistent, and coe_sup is correctly left non-simp. Nothing was run in Lean. I did not check that the added attribute on coeToSubmodule_eq_bot is confluent with the other rules, so I mention it only as a minor point. The main finding is the duplicated mem_coeSubmodule, which I read directly in both files.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp] -- Ensure `simp` is confluent for `x ∈ ((I : Ideal R) : FractionalIdeal S P)`.
theorem mem_coeSubmodule {x : P} {I : Ideal R} :
    x ∈ coeSubmodule P I ↔ ∃ x', x' ∈ I ∧ algebraMap R P x' = x :=
  Iff.rfl
findings.problem: The simp lemma for membership in `coeSubmodule` is a duplicate in the wrong namespace and file. `IsLocalization.mem_coeSubmodule` already states exactly this and is not `@[simp]`. `FractionalIdeal.mem_coeSubmodule` adds the same statement under the same short name. The file opens `IsLocalization`, so the bare name `mem_coeSubmodule` is ambiguous there. This is why the proof of `mem_coeIdeal` uses `mem_coeSubmodule _ _` and the new lemma takes no explicit arguments. The simp rule about `IsLocalization.coeSubmodule` belongs with that definition, not in the FractionalIdeal API. As it stands, `simp` unfolds `x ∈ coeSubmodule P I` for FractionalIdeal users only. Users of other files that import `Localization.Submodule` don't get it.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `IsLocalization.mem_coeSubmodule` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Submodule.lean` as `@[simp]`, with its `I` argument explicit as now. Delete `FractionalIdeal.mem_coeSubmodule` here and keep the confluence comment next to `mem_coeIdeal` or `coe_coeIdeal`. Keep `mem_coeIdeal` as is, since it is the form that applies to `x ∈ (↑I : FractionalIdeal S P)`.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical simp lemma for `coeSubmodule` membership, with no ambiguous-name risk after `open IsLocalization`. Other files that use `coeSubmodule` also get the simp rewrite. The FractionalIdeal namespace stops carrying a lemma that is not about fractional ideals.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem mem_coeSubmodule (I : Ideal R) {x : S} :
    x ∈ coeSubmodule S I ↔ ∃ y : R, y ∈ I ∧ algebraMap R S y = x :=
  Iff.rfl

findings.excerpt:
@[norm_cast]
theorem coe_nsmul (n : ℕ) (I : FractionalIdeal S P) :
    (↑(n • I) : Submodule R P) = n • (I : Submodule R P) :=
  rfl
findings.problem: The other coercion lemmas for the semiring structure (`coe_zero`, `coe_one`, `coe_add`, `coe_mul`, `coe_pow`) are tagged `@[simp, norm_cast]`. `coe_nsmul` and `coe_natCast` (line 607) are only `@[norm_cast]` (`coe_natCast` has no attribute). `↑(n • I)` and `↑(n : FractionalIdeal S P)` therefore do not simplify to their submodule forms, although both lemmas are used as the `commSemiring` fields. The ring-hom data are therefore only partly simp-covered. The lemmas are unused elsewhere in RingTheory, and I found no uses elsewhere in Mathlib, so this is a minor gap.
findings.proposed_change: Change the attributes to `@[simp, norm_cast]` on `coe_nsmul`. Add the same to `coe_natCast`, which has no attribute at all. Check that the RHS `n • ↑I` and the natural-number cast on submodules stay in simp normal form.
findings.benefit: All coercions of the `CommSemiring` operations then simplify consistently. Users can reduce `↑(n • I)` and `↑(n : FractionalIdeal S P)` with `simp` instead of unfolding them by hand.
